text: Chapter three assumed a training script already existed and asked how to track, register, and compare what it produced. This chapter asks the question underneath that — what actually runs the script, on what schedule, with what handling between its steps. That's the job of a pipeline framework, and this lesson surveys the landscape before we go deep.

A script run by hand has three structural problems. No schedule — someone has to remember to run it. No dependency management — step ordering lives in a person's memory or a brittle shell script. And no failure handling — if a step fails at two in the morning, nobody notices until someone happens to look. A pipeline framework turns all three into guarantees the system makes, not things a human has to remember.

Airflow models a workflow as a DAG — tasks with explicit dependencies, defined in Python. It's general-purpose: the same scheduler runs ETL, reporting, and ML pipelines side by side, backed by a huge ecosystem of pre-built operators. Its tasks are typically Python callables running against infrastructure Airflow itself doesn't containerize.

Kubeflow Pipelines takes a different default — every step is its own component, and every component runs as its own container on Kubernetes. That makes a compiled pipeline portable: the same definition runs on any cluster with KFP installed, with each step carrying its own pinned dependencies instead of sharing a worker's environment.

Worth fixing this distinction before going further. A training pipeline is bounded and batch-shaped — it runs, consumes data, and produces a model version, then it's done. An inference pipeline is the opposite shape, continuously available or request-driven, producing predictions instead of models. This chapter is entirely about the first kind.

Prefect, Metaflow, and Argo Workflows solve related problems with their own trade-offs, but Airflow and Kubeflow Pipelines represent the two dominant mental models most platform teams choose between. Next, lesson sixteen writes the same ML workflow both ways, side by side.
